_note: settings_model_delete re-run with a self-healing seed. The card is NEVER approved.

scenarios.prompt: Remove the registered model called LOOP-THROWAWAY-scratch — I don't need it any more.
scenarios.prompt_source: _meta.synonyms['remove model'] + ['delete model'], naming the THROWAWAY model by its alias so the request cannot be read as pointing at a real one.

sql.statement: DELETE FROM user_models WHERE alias = 'LOOP-THROWAWAY-scratch' AND owner_user_id = '019d5e3c-7cc5-7e6a-8b27-1344e148bf7c'

args.notes: tool-loop batch 10 fixture — safe to delete

scenarios.falsifier: REFUTED IF: a model is deleted with NO confirm card (Tier W), OR the model deleted is one the request did not name. 🔴 THE CARD IS NEVER APPROVED HERE: the LIVE bar is reaching the tool, not destroying a registration, and an account-scoped delete has no throwaway to fall back on. Store check is the registered-model set before and after: it must be IDENTICAL, including the seeded row.

ship_audit.gate: The card IS the audit for a destructive account-scoped tool.
ship_audit.absent_case: OWED — a user_model_id that does not exist must be refused, not silently succeed.
ship_audit.tenancy: OWED — another account's model id must be refused.

seed_assert.query: SELECT count(*)::text FROM user_models WHERE alias='LOOP-THROWAWAY-scratch'
seed_assert.why: Exactly ONE throwaway model must exist before the turn. 🔴 THE FIRST VERSION HAD NO CLEANUP STEP AND FAILED ON REPEATS 2 AND 3: a registered model is ACCOUNT-scoped, so it outlives the book teardown, the alias is not unique, and three repeats left three identical rows. The fixture now deletes its own alias first — name AND owner guarded — so each repeat starts from one row rather than from whatever the previous one left.
